title: AutoCiteWikidata :Making Automatic Citations Connected with Wikidata
content:
Adding a citation to Wikipedia has become much easier over the years. VisualEditor’s automatic citation tool can often turn an ISBN, DOI, or web address into a formatted reference in just a few clicks, largely thanks to its integration with Zotero.

But there is another source of bibliographic information that Wikimedia editors increasingly have at their disposal: Wikidata.

Could Wikidata make automatic citations more connected, reusable, and easier to maintain?

AutoCiteWikidata is an attempt to explore that possibility.

When we find a useful source online, we often copy its URL into the citation tool. This works well when the web page contains good bibliographic metadata. But sometimes the result describes the web page rather than the work itself.

A scanned book on Internet Archive, for example, is still a book. A research paper accessed through a publisher’s website is still a journal article.

Ideally, the citation should identify the book or article, including its author, title, publisher or journal, publication date, volume, pages, and other available identifiers—not merely the website where we found it.

This is where Wikidata can help.

title: OpenAI “rogue” agent activities found on Wikimedia projects
content:
Recently, multiple organisations have disclosed how clusters of so-called “rogue” AI agents attempted to break into websites and online services, sometimes successfully. Agents from OpenAI’s environment, in particular, are known to have used other public wikis (collaboratively edited websites not owned by us) to communicate and coordinate with each other.

These types of successful intrusions can expose sensitive data or disrupt website services that users rely on, while clusters of agents can attempt attacks at a scale that is difficult for defenders to manage. They affect people behind the websites who may not understand the nature of the attack, or have the tools to effectively fight back. For a site like Wikipedia, agents might find and use security vulnerabilities or make misleading edits at scale. Wikipedia’s volunteer editors and the Wikimedia Foundation’s security teams have to detect and undo that activity.

title: How Wiki Loves Earth’s images expressed love in 2026
content:
If humanity truly wants to understand the meaning of love, we must look to nature and animals to see how love is instinctively formed, and how feelings arise without words. Nature has taught us profound lessons without speaking to us directly, simply observing the behavior of the creatures around us is enough to reveal the meanings of loyalty, care, attachment, and love.

This is precisely what I noticed while contemplating the results of Wiki Loves Earth 2026. In some of the images, I saw more than just documentation of nature; I saw scenes that reminded us, as humans, of what it means to love instinctively.

title: Adventures, Comrades, and Endless Memories: My Wikimedia CEE Meeting Impressions
content:
International conferences are never just about formal sessions and presentations. My journey to the Wikimedia CEE Meeting 2026 in Cluj-Napoca, Romania, gave me far more than professional experience, it brought me lifelong memories, funny moments, and unforgettable friendships.

My trip kicked off on September 16th with a night flight. During the layover in Istanbul, I had the wonderful chance to meet members of the Georgian Wikimedia community and received a special gift for the Turkic Marathon. But international travel rarely goes smoothly… Upon arriving in Cluj, my luggage was severely damaged and practically unusable, and to top it all off, I accidentally checked into the wrong hotel!

Because of these minor misadventures, I arrived at the Learning Day a bit late. From the very first minutes, my inner paparazzo kicked in, and I started capturing my new acquaintance, Nal Mencin, on camera, a habit that continued right up until the end of the conference.

title: From Local Contributions to a Global Movement: My Wikimania 2026 Journey
content:
For me, Wikimania 2026 was not simply a conference in Paris. It was a journey that connected many parts of my Wikimedia experience – learning, volunteering, meeting people from different communities, exploring new ideas, and contributing to the free knowledge movement in my own way.

When I received the opportunity to attend Wikimania 2026 in Paris, I knew that this would be a very different experience from participating in Wikimedia activities from Odisha. Wikimania brought together Wikimedians from different countries, languages, backgrounds, and communities. The 2026 edition was held from 21 to 25 July at the Cité des Sciences et de l’Industrie in Paris, under the theme “Freedom, Equity, Reliability.” It was also a special year because Wikipedia was celebrating its 25th anniversary.

Coming to Paris for my second Wikimania was a very different experience. This time, I was not completely new to the Wikimedia community. I already knew some people from my previous Wikimania experience and from my interactions within the movement, while many others were new faces whose work and communities I was getting to know for the first time.

title: Recording History Across the Four Sultanates of Moloku Kie Raha – The WikiRempah Journey: Ternate Part
content:
The Spice Route of the Indonesian archipelago is more than just an entry in history books; it is a cultural heritage whose traces can still be followed today. Born from the realization of the importance of documenting these historic sites, the WikiRempah Project focuses on recording Spice Route cultural sites—particularly in Eastern Indonesia, a region rich in history yet lacking in documentation.

For this leg of the journey, the WikiRempah team traveled across North Maluku, specifically visiting the four great sultanates known collectively as Moloku Kie Raha. Our route began in Ternate, continued to Tidore and Jailolo, and concluded in Bacan.

title: Activating the Setswana Language for Wikipedia 25: Digital Milestones and Community Growth in Botswana
content:
WIKIPEDIA 25: SETSWANA KNOWLAGE ACTIVATION

As the global Wikimedia movement aligns to celebrate Wikipedia 25, regional affiliates and user groups are critically evaluating the strategic frameworks required to build sustainable digital footprints for underrepresented languages. In Botswana, this milestone was marked by the execution of the Wikipedia 25: Setswana Knowledge Activation Campaign. Organized by WikiVerse Botswana, the initiative aimed to address systemic biases in the open-knowledge ecosystem by accelerating content depth and structural quality on the Setswana Wikipedia (tn.wikipedia.org).

Rather than evaluating success through raw data alone, this report focuses on the core qualitative breakthroughs, operational frameworks, and critical structural learnings derived from the activation. These insights establish a scalable blueprint for regional language preservation and community governance.
creator: Mothusi Sekhomba

title: Apply For Scholarship Now: Shape the Future of ESEAP at the ESEAP Strategy Summit 2027!
content:
The Wikimedia East, Southeast Asia, and the Pacific (ESEAP) region, in collaboration with the Wikimedians of Japan User Group (WJPUG) and the ESEAP Hub, is delighted to announce that applications for the ESEAP Strategy Summit 2027 are now open!

The Wikimedia ESEAP Strategy Summit is a three-day meeting for Wikimedians in the ESEAP region to discuss the Movement Strategy and the ongoing evolution of the ESEAP Hub. The 2027 summit, which was the first one since the ESEAP hub was formally established, is aimed to foster new leaders within region and a strategic space to discuss future support for ESEAP related and based volunteers

The Summit is expected to meet the following objectives:

  • Bringing together ESEAP leaders to accelerate ESEAP contribution to Wikimedia Movement.
  • Transitioning from governance design to practical operationalisation and capacity building to support content development in various Wikiprojects by the affiliates.
  • Supporting the inclusion of emerging communities, language diversity, and easier access for newcomers such as presence in ESEAP and global movement.
  • Strengthening peer-to-peer mentorship and collaborative projects in ESEAP.

title: Day Two at the Language Diversity Conference 2026: From Language and AI to Community Action
content:
The second day of the Language Diversity Conference 2026 continued today, Saturday, 3 October, in Accra with another full program of discussions, workshops, and practical sessions focused on the future of languages in the digital world.

It’s the first Saturday of the month, which in Ghana means national clean-up day: shops close, and people spend the morning tidying up their neighbourhoods. If the Ghanaians in the room had been at home, they’d have been out cleaning too.

There was a quick word about the food, too. So far we’d been served peppers in red, green, and black, the colours of the Ghanaian flag. The yellow ones? Still to come. Different shapes and different colours, a bit like everyone in the room.

Then it was down to business and to a question that has been hanging over this conference since day one: what does AI mean for the languages people here are working so hard to keep alive?

title: Global GLAM Calls: A Community Space for Cultural Heritage and Wikimedia
content:
The Wikimedia Movement depends on its relationships with cultural heritage institutions around the world, and the GLAM (Galleries, Libraries, Archives, and Museums) community is at the heart of that story. Whether they’re hosting editathons or providing primary reference material for Wikipedia content, these organizations share our mission and values, and they make it possible to expand free knowledge everywhere.

Since 2024, the GLAM community has been getting together for regular online meetups to swap ideas, talk through projects, and share success stories from this work. It’s a chance to learn from each other and to celebrate what’s happening in libraries, museums, and archives across the movement.

This year, the calls had a new helping hand: the Content Partnerships Hub, a consortium project of nine Wikimedia affiliates dedicated to supporting everyone in the movement who works with content partners. Their involvement means more outreach to the community to build agendas that reflect what people actually want to discuss, plus a structured foundation that helps the calls keep growing.

title: Wikimedia Affiliations Committee Has New Officers and Advisors
content:
The Wikimedia Affiliations Committee (AffCom) has begun a new chapter, with changes to its leadership and the addition of new advisors.

AffCom is the committee that advises the Wikimedia Foundation Board of Trustees on the recognition and continued existence of Wikimedia movement affiliates, including chapters, thematic organisations, and user groups.

Following the latest appointments in July 2026, the officers are: Mari Avetisyan as Chair, Harriet Bayel as Vice-Chair, Johnny Alegre as Secretary, and Robert Jamal as Treasurer.

The four officers bring experience from different parts of the Wikimedia movement and regions of the world. Together with the other voting members, they will support the Committee’s ongoing work on affiliate governance, conflict resolution, and the development of the affiliate ecosystem.

AffCom’s voting members are supported by non-voting advisors, who contribute experience, language skills, institutional knowledge, and governance expertise. Advisors can take part in Committee discussions and subcommittee meetings, offering additional perspectives on the Committee’s work.
snippet: The Wikimedia Affiliations Committee (AffCom) has begun a new chapter, with changes to its leadership and the addition of new advisors.
creator: Mari Avetisyan WMAM

title: Climate Change and Free Knowledge: Workshops for Editing Urgent Issues
content: Together, as a community, and with climate change activists, we held the CC+CL (Climate Change and Open Knowledge) workshops. On Friday, September 11, we came together to explore a topic that is rarely discussed in conjunction: free knowledge and environmental conflicts through actions aimed at climate justice. The virtual session brought together young environmental activists from the Bolivian Platform for Action on Climate Change (PBACC, spanish acronym), who arrived with questions and a strong desire to understand what Wikipedia has to do with the struggles they face every day. We discussed the Wikimedia Foundation and its projects, with a special focus on Wikipedia, that encyclopedia we all use but few of us dare to question or advocate for. We began by debunking some common misconceptions —such as that Wikipedia “isn’t serious” or “anyone can write anything,” among others— and explained how it really works: creating an account, the review mechanisms, and the importance of sources. It was a necessary introduction, designed as a prelude to what would come the following day.

title: Wiki Loves Arbërësh: an expedition to document the Albanian diaspora heritage in Sicily
content:
At the end of September 2026, a small crew of Wikipedia volunteers in Sicily, Italy, went to Piana degli Albanesi, a town near Palermo. Our goal: document and highlight the cultural heritage of this community on the Wikimedia projects.

Piana degli Albanesi (Hora e Arbëreshëvet) has a very particular culture, as the most important centre of the Arbëresh community of Sicily, that preserved many traditions from the Albanian diaspora since the 15th century: from the Byzantine-Catholic churches to traditional costumes, and the Arbëresh language, classified as endangered by UNESCO.

Staying in Piana for a weekend was a wonderful experience: we received a warm welcome from the town’s residents, who went out of their way to help us visit and document as many places as possible in just a few days, and who shared the unique aspects of their culture with us with passion and pride.

On top of talking to people to get a grasp of the history and challenges of the Arbëresh community, we wanted to gather as much content as possible to release under a free license on the Wikimedia projects, so it could be available to everyone online and contribute to preserving the Arbëresh living heritage.

title: WikiRempah Overcomes Challenges in Tidore for Training and Documentation of Historic Sites
content:
After Wikimedia Indonesia organized WikiLatih for students in Tidore in 2019, the WikiRempah team aimed to continue its efforts to spread knowledge. The initiative, led by Ana Ainina, Supardi Sahabu, and Sofi Solihah, was funded by Rapid Fund Wikimedia Foundation.

Finding partners in Tidore presented a unique challenge for us. There is a time difference of about two hours between the team’s location and Tidore, so we had to adjust our communication process accordingly. In the early stages, we searched for potential partners via machine learning and reached out one by one to local literacy communities that might be interested in collaborating.

We also leveraged our existing inter-community networks and even expanded our search through connections within government circles. However, differences in age and communication styles required us to adjust our approach.
